case_title: SHAHAJA @ SHAHAJAN ISMAIL MOHD. SHAIKH v. STATE OF MAHARASHTRA
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were labourers working in the Vile Parle area of Mumbai. A quarrel between them occurred on the night of 10.12.2006 near the Vile Parle Railway Station. The accused assaulted the victim with a hammer on his head, resulting in the victim's death. The victim's brother and another witness reported witnessing the assault. The victim's body was found the next morning, and a post-mortem examination revealed severe head injuries. The hammer used in the assault was recovered and found to be stained with the victim's blood. The trial court convicted the accused based on the eyewitness accounts and the discovery of the weapon. The High Court upheld the conviction, but the Supreme Court ultimately acquitted the accused, finding that the eyewitness accounts and discovery of the weapon were not sufficient to establish guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.
